summary.intent: Continue and complete the CipherBox Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability) workflow: audit/retire stale todos, plan/execute/verify/ship Phase 72, while also firefighting unrelated CI regressions (web-e2e, desktop-e2e, sdk-e2e) discovered mid-flow and resolving web-e2e flakiness as a priority.
summary.outcome: Phase 72 was fully planned (research+patterns+10 plans), executed across 7 waves with TDD, hardened (all test-file TS drift fixed, CI now typechecks tests, a real DoS cycle-guard bug found and fixed), verified, and shipped as PR #602 with CI green; two CI regressions were fixed and merged (PR #601 FUSE seq-equivocation + D-16 driver fix, PR #600 web-e2e floor helper + sdk-e2e Test 21 + flake fixes); a security review found and the team fixed a HIGH-severity moveItem write-chain resurrection gap before merge, with PR review triage still in progress at transcript end.

repo: `ci-e2e.yml` (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or `workflow_dispatch`, never on PRs — must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on older workflow definitions) to validate before merging.

Playwright `ciFloor()` helper raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor only under CI (`process.env.CI`); local runs use much tighter timeouts (15-30s), causing IPNS-gated mutation tests to flake locally on a cold/loaded stack even though they pass in CI.

`webServer.reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI` in playwright.config.ts means setting CI=1 locally to get the 60s floor conflicts with reusing an already-running dev stack — must temporarily patch reuse to true to combine both.
vitest ignores `.env` files — test harnesses reading `process.env.SDK_E2E_SECRET` need it explicitly exported in the shell, or they silently fall back to a default test secret and get 401s.

Cross-package `@cipherbox/*` imports resolve via workspace symlinks to each package's built `dist`, not path aliases/project references — so typecheck must run build-first per package in dependency order (crypto→core→api-client→sdk-core→sdk).

Root `pnpm typecheck` (CI's Typecheck job) only ran `tsconfig.build.json` per package, which excludes test files — test-file TypeScript errors never surfaced in CI until this phase added test-inclusive `tsc --noEmit` scripts.

IPNS anti-equivocation gate (Phase 71, ipns.service.ts) rejects same-sequence republish with a different CID (400) — FUSE's per-file publish path must resolve-before-first-publish rather than hardcoding seq=1, or it collides with this gate on rotation re-keys.
Phase 71 (#599) shipped with drift: DTO field renames (readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName) not propagated to desktop-e2e `.mts` test drivers.

`dfsFindFolder` in client.ts uses a `visited: Set<string>` cycle guard; `collectDescendantIpnsNames` lacked the same guard, allowing unbounded recursion on a cyclic/malicious folder graph (DoS-class) — same guard pattern now applied to all 3 call sites.

`updateFolderMetadataAndPublish`'s write-body merge falls back to a naive union (resurrecting dropped WriteChildRefs on CAS retry) unless callers explicitly pass `baseWriteChildren` — `deleteItem` and `restoreFromBin`/`permanentDeleteFromBin` were fixed in this phase but `moveItem`'s source-folder publish was initially missed despite dropping a WriteChildRef the same way.

`shared-write.ts` (deleteFromSharedFolder/moveInSharedFolder for actual shared folders) has the same missing-baseWriteChildren exposure but was out of this phase's diff — pre-existing, deferred as a todo.

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the first-publish branch; fixed to resolve IPNS first and route into CAS retry (with pre-resolved seq passed through) if a record is Found, avoiding equivocation with Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate.

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (Greptile P2 perf fix) so the Found path in content_ops.rs doesn't redundantly re-resolve sequence; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since pre-resolved becomes stale after a conflict.
collectDescendantIpnsNames added a shared visited Set across recursive calls/root call sites to guard against cyclic folder graphs causing unbounded recursion (DoS).

getWriteBodyParams unified into single shared implementation (was duplicated in client.ts and bin/index.ts); fails closed (throws) on a genuine null IPNS resolve when a real writeKey is present, but short-circuits before that for zero/absent writeKey read-only fallback.

Base-aware CAS-merge logic: prunes a childId present in baseWriteChildren but absent locally (even if a racing writer's stale remote snapshot still has it), while still admitting genuinely concurrent remote-only adds — the core mechanism deleteItem/restoreFromBin/moveItem must all thread baseWriteChildren through to avoid resurrecting dropped WriteChildRefs.

moveItem's source-folder publish dropped the moved child's WriteChildRef via filter() but never passed baseWriteChildren to updateFolderMetadataAndPublish, exposing it to the naive-union resurrection bug fixed elsewhere in this phase; fixed by capturing sourceBaseWriteChildren before the drop and threading it through (destination publish left as add-only, no base needed).

workflow: When a background local test run keeps cascading on ambient/unrelated flakes (never reaching the target tests), running under the CI-equivalent timeout regime (e.g. CI=1 to engage timeout floors) rather than repeatedly bumping individual local timeouts is the faster path to a representative pass/fail signal.
Deferring hardening work (test-file typecheck fixes, CI wiring) to the end of a multi-wave phase lets one pass cover both pre-existing drift and all newly-added test files, avoiding rework each wave.

When multiple subagents might touch the same file (e.g. client.ts) sequentially, explicitly holding/serializing dispatches (waiting for one to finish before starting the next) avoids merge conflicts, at the cost of losing parallelism.

Spawning a dedicated crypto/security-reviewer agent scoped to a diff, even after unit/e2e gates pass, surfaced a real HIGH-severity write-chain vulnerability (moveItem resurrection) that no automated test or CodeRabbit run had caught — worth doing before merge on any phase touching key/write-chain logic.

Verified-landed commit false-negatives (commit tool reports timeout/failure while `git log` shows it actually succeeded) recurred multiple times this session — always confirm via `git log --oneline -1` rather than retrying blindly.

friction: Multiple rounds of local Playwright verification runs were derailed by different ambient flakes each time (4.10 batch delete, 4.11 batch move, 2.1 create-folder) at increasing levels of load on the dev machine, before switching to a CI-equivalent timeout regime to get a clean signal — cost significant wall-clock time.

GSD hook JSON files contain raw/control characters in string values that broke standard JSON parsing (`gh`/jq-style extraction), requiring a custom lenient parser script to extract research/planner-contribution fragments.
Stale API process on :3000 served an outdated TEST_LOGIN_SECRET/dist build multiple times, causing spurious 401s in sdk-e2e runs until manually killed and restarted from source.
vitest not loading .env caused a silent SDK_E2E_SECRET fallback mismatch (401s) that required a non-obvious diagnosis (checksum comparison) before the fix (explicit env export) was found.
`gh workflow run -f ref=` returned an HTTP 422 because main's workflow definition predated the `ref` input, requiring the `--ref <branch>` flag form instead.

Confusing/contradictory git state checks (cat-file appearing to disagree with git status) briefly caused doubt about whether todo-move commits had landed correctly; resolved by a more decisive HEAD-tree check.
CodeRabbit CLI and a dedicated security-reviewer agent both needed to run and be reconciled against each other, adding coordination overhead to the ship-phase step.
